dedupe_keys.name: health and environmental evaluation of barcelona s first superblocks salut als carrers

description: Barcelona's superblocks reorganise streets to reverse the split of public space between vehicles and people, reducing space for private cars and reclaiming it for residents to cut air pollution, traffic injuries and sedentary behaviour and add green space. The Salut als Carrers (Health in the Streets) project of the city Public Health Agency evaluated the environmental and health effects of the first three superblocks with an equity perspective. The 2020 protocol describes quasi-experimental and health impact assessment methods including a pre-post health survey of 1,200 randomly selected residents; the 2025 results paper combines the survey with air quality measurements, the MAPS pedestrian audit, SOPARC observation of physical activity, ethnographic studies and focus groups. Coverage: the Sant Antoni, Poblenou and Horta superblocks. Access: open-access articles and a Partnership for Healthy Cities summary (2021). Licence: CC-BY-4.0 articles. Caveats: data are available only on request, and agency authors work for the city body responsible for superblocks. Simulation uses: evidence for modelling health effects of street space reallocation. Related records: the Getxo green space benefit-cost analysis.
